Bidding exactly $6 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the competition's exit points, and I pay only the second-highest bid, never overpaying relative to my value. Since this functions as a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I'd pay the competitor's bid, not my own. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, truthful bidding is optimal.
